unanchored.title: Audit chain not anchored
unanchored.body: The audit chain is consistent with itself, but the stop witness could not confirm where it ends, so rows cut from the end cannot be ruled out. The numbers below are shown, but do not treat this run as verified.

reason.no_witness: There is no stop witness for this run, so there is nothing to compare the chain with.
reason.no_witness_record: The stop witness has no record for this run yet, so the end of the chain could not be confirmed.
reason.witness_unreadable: The stop witness could not be read (it is missing, damaged or being written), so the end of the chain could not be confirmed.
reason.behind_witness: The chain ends before the point the stop witness recorded: the end of the audit chain has been cut off.

ui6SetVault.title: Vault keyring
ui6SetVault.about: This computer has no system keychain, so the key that encrypts your vault (API keys, logins) is kept in a file protected by a passphrase. The app can't ask for that passphrase while it works, so saving a secret fails until you save the passphrase here. It is stored in a file only your user account can read.

ui6SetBudget.title: AI task budgets
ui6SetBudget.about: Spend caps for tasks handed to the coder. A task runs under the lowest cap that applies to it and never above the coder budget {{budget}}. A cap of 0 means no spend, never unlimited, and with no cap at all a task does not run. Tasks and the agents they start count against the same caps. Only you raise a cap; an agent can only lower its own.
ui6SetBudget.per_agent_hint: A conversation is one coder chat, with the workers it starts; a role is a kind of worker.

ui6SetHelp.firstSteps_blurb: Sign in, make a profile, run something harmless.
ui6SetHelp.firstSteps_quip: Everyone starts with zero profiles. It is a very relaxed starting line.
ui6SetHelp.firstSteps_s1: Sign in to monoes.me first: MonoAgent needs an account before anything runs. In a terminal, run monoagentcli account login.
ui6SetHelp.firstSteps_s2: Create a profile: the dashboard shows what happens inside one. Run monoagentcli profile create <name>, or use the dashboard.
ui6SetHelp.firstSteps_s3: Start from a template and press Run. The hello template needs no credentials: monoagentcli workflow templates run hello --profile <name>.
ui6SetHelp.firstSteps_s4: Hid the get-started checklist and want it back? This brings it back on the dashboard.
ui6SetHelp.profiles_blurb: Everything you own lives in a profile, and every call names it.
ui6SetHelp.profiles_quip: There is no default profile. Yes, you will type --profile a lot. It keeps your accounts from meeting each other at parties.
ui6SetHelp.profiles_s1: A profile holds its own sessions, credentials, workflows, vault and people. Commands that act on one take --profile <id|name>.
ui6SetHelp.profiles_s2: List yours with monoagentcli profile list, and see what one holds with monoagentcli profile context --profile <name>.
ui6SetHelp.profiles_s3: Machine-wide commands (version, update, config, account) do not take a profile.
ui6SetHelp.connections_blurb: Link a platform once; workflows reuse it.
ui6SetHelp.connections_quip: Credentials go in the vault, not in a sticky note. The vault appreciates the compliment.
ui6SetHelp.connections_s1: Open Connections to see which platforms you have saved and how each one connects.
ui6SetHelp.connections_s2: From a terminal, monoagentcli connect list --all shows every supported platform, and monoagentcli connect show <platform> shows its methods and fields.
ui6SetHelp.connections_s3: Test a saved connection with monoagentcli connect test <platform> to re-validate its credentials. Web automations run in your own browser through the extension, so log in there too.
ui6SetHelp.workflows_blurb: Build it once, run it whenever.
ui6SetHelp.workflows_quip: A workflow is a recipe. A template is a recipe someone else already burnt the first batch of.
ui6SetHelp.workflows_s1: Pick a template and press Run. Browse them in the workflow editor.
ui6SetHelp.workflows_s2: From a terminal, monoagentcli workflow templates list shows the bundled templates and monoagentcli workflow templates show <id> shows inputs and the exact run command.
ui6SetHelp.workflows_s3: Schedules and webhooks need the background service: monoagentcli daemon keeps them alive in the foreground.
ui6SetHelp.workflows_s4: Ask a coder agent to build one for you, then validate it before the first run.
ui6SetHelp.workflows_s4_prompt: Using the monoagent-build skill, create a workflow in my profile that runs every weekday at 09:00 and saves a short summary of my unread messages to the task board. Look up the node types and their schemas first, validate the workflow, run it once and show me each node's output before enabling the schedule.
ui6SetHelp.tasks_blurb: A kanban board for you and your AI agents.
ui6SetHelp.tasks_quip: Moving a card to Ready is how you tell an agent "go on, then". Moving it back is how you change your mind.
ui6SetHelp.tasks_s1: The board has five columns. New tasks land in the Inbox, and you approve them to Ready, where an AI agent may take them.
ui6SetHelp.tasks_s2: Add one from a terminal: monoagentcli task add "<title>" --profile <name> (add --ready to skip the Inbox).
ui6SetHelp.tasks_s3: Agents hand work back for review. You verify it or send it back; nothing is done until you say so.
ui6SetHelp.hil_blurb: Anything an agent wants to send waits for your yes.
ui6SetHelp.hil_quip: The Approve button is deliberately boring. Boring buttons are safe buttons.
ui6SetHelp.hil_s1: Pending approvals show up in Communications. Read the card, then approve or reject.
ui6SetHelp.hil_s2: From a terminal, monoagentcli hil list shows what is waiting, and monoagentcli hil approve or hil reject answers one.
ui6SetHelp.hil_s3: A HIL step with no timeout waits forever (the default timeout is 0, which means unlimited), so a run and its context sit parked until someone answers. Set timeout_minutes if that matters to you.
ui6SetHelp.hil_s4: auto_decide lets Jev approve items it is confident about on your behalf. It needs Jev enabled for approvals; check its settings before relying on it.
ui6SetHelp.hil_danger: Auto-approve means a polite wrong guess goes out as you. Review what it decided at least once.
ui6SetHelp.orgs_blurb: Teams of agents with roles, budgets and a boss.
ui6SetHelp.orgs_quip: You are the board of directors. The agents are very keen interns.
ui6SetHelp.orgs_s1: Orgs and agents need monomind initialized in this profile's folder first.
ui6SetHelp.orgs_s2: Open an org to see its chart, spend and pending approvals.
ui6SetHelp.orgs_s3: Ask a coder agent to design one for a specific job.
ui6SetHelp.orgs_s3_prompt: Create an org in my profile named "inbox-triage" with a boss role and two worker roles: one that reads new messages and drafts replies, one that files tasks on my task board. Keep autonomy on manual so every send waits for my approval, set a small budget, validate the org and show me the role chart before running it.
ui6SetHelp.orgs_danger: A role with full access is an employee with your house key who never clocks out, limited only by budgets. Keep roles scoped.
ui6SetHelp.coderModes_blurb: Off, mission or open-ended: pick before the first message.
ui6SetHelp.coderModes_quip: The mode is chosen before you say hello and cannot change afterwards. Choose like you are picking a haircut.
ui6SetHelp.coderModes_s1: Coder mode is off until you turn it on in Settings. From a terminal, monoagentcli coder status shows where it stands.
ui6SetHelp.coderModes_s2: Chat modes: Off is a plain chat. Mission means the lead plans the work and goes on until you close it. Open-ended runs until you stop it.
ui6SetHelp.coderModes_s3: Open-ended is offered only while the coder binding is on and can start on this machine; the chat will tell you why if it cannot.
ui6SetHelp.coderModes_s4: Raise a chat's access level one step at a time: scoped, coding, workspace, full. Only you can raise it.
ui6SetHelp.coderModes_s5: Not sure where to start? Ask a coder chat to walk the settings with you.
ui6SetHelp.coderModes_s5_prompt: Run monoagentcli coder status and monoagentcli doctor, then explain in plain language what coder mode would be allowed to do on this machine and which default access level new chats would get. Do not enable anything; just report and recommend settings.
ui6SetHelp.coderModes_danger: Coder mode on means the agent can run any command and change any file as you. Start at the lowest level that does the job.
ui6SetHelp.extension_blurb: Lets MonoAgent drive your own browser.
ui6SetHelp.extension_quip: It works inside your real browser, so your logins come along. That is the feature and the warning in one sentence.
ui6SetHelp.extension_s1: Install: monoagentcli extension install unpacks the bridge extension for your browser; load it as an unpacked extension.
ui6SetHelp.extension_s2: Pair: monoagentcli extension pair prints the token to paste into the extension side panel.
ui6SetHelp.extension_s3: Check: monoagentcli extension status says whether a bridge is running and the extension is attached.
ui6SetHelp.extension_s4: Limit what agents may do in it with monoagentcli browser permissions set <kind|all> <level>. Levels, mildest first: off, ask, dev, full, full-no-approvals.
ui6SetHelp.extension_danger: A paired browser is not restricted to particular profiles by default. Restrict it if more than one person or agent can reach the token.
ui6SetHelp.vault_blurb: Passwords and logins, encrypted, referenced by name.
ui6SetHelp.vault_quip: Agents get to use a secret without seeing it. That is not distrust, it is good manners.
ui6SetHelp.vault_s1: Add secrets and logins in the Secrets vault; list shows metadata only, never values.
ui6SetHelp.vault_s2: Agent access defaults to strict. use lets an agent use secrets without retrieving plaintext; reveal lets it read them. Set it with monoagentcli secret agent-access strict|use|reveal.
ui6SetHelp.vault_s3: Every agent read is audited by name, never by value: monoagentcli secret agent-access audit.
ui6SetHelp.vault_danger: Reveal lets an agent read your passwords in plaintext. Scope it by secret, host and expiry, or leave it on strict.
ui6SetHelp.apiGateway_blurb: An OpenAI-compatible endpoint with keys you control.
ui6SetHelp.apiGateway_quip: It listens on your machine only, unless you say otherwise. Say otherwise carefully.
ui6SetHelp.apiGateway_s1: Check where it listens and whether it answers: monoagentcli api status --profile <name>.
ui6SetHelp.apiGateway_s2: Create a key (shown once): monoagentcli api key create --profile <name>. Revoke it any time with api key revoke.
ui6SetHelp.apiGateway_s3: List the models the gateway would serve: monoagentcli api models.
ui6SetHelp.images_blurb: Generate pictures and keep them in one place.
ui6SetHelp.images_quip: The media vault does not judge your 47 versions of the same wizard.
ui6SetHelp.images_s1: Generated and added images, audio and video live in the media vault.
ui6SetHelp.images_s2: Log in to Gemini once with monoagentcli login gemini, then run the single-image template: monoagentcli workflow templates run gemimg --input '{"prompt":"a red bicycle"}' --profile <name>.
ui6SetHelp.images_s3: Browse from a terminal with monoagentcli media list --profile <name>.
ui6SetHelp.troubleshooting_blurb: Something is off? Ask the doctor first.
ui6SetHelp.troubleshooting_quip: The doctor does not say "have you tried turning it off and on again" until it has actually checked.
ui6SetHelp.troubleshooting_s1: Run monoagentcli doctor to check everything MonoAgent needs on this machine, and monoagentcli doctor --fix to apply the fixes.
ui6SetHelp.troubleshooting_s2: Read the logs for what actually happened.
ui6SetHelp.troubleshooting_s3: monoagentcli status gives an overview, and monoagentcli summary lists what needs your attention.
ui6SetHelp.troubleshooting_s4: Still stuck? Hand the diagnosis to a coder agent.
ui6SetHelp.troubleshooting_s4_prompt: Run monoagentcli doctor and monoagentcli status, read the most recent errors in the logs, and tell me what is wrong and the smallest fix. Apply only fixes that doctor marks as automatic, and ask me before anything else.
ui6SetHelp.updates_quip: New versions arrive often. Checking costs nothing; installing is your call.
ui6SetHelp.updates_s1: See what you run and whether a newer release exists in Settings.
ui6SetHelp.updates_s2: From a terminal, monoagentcli update --check only reports; monoagentcli update installs.
ui6SetHelp.pit1_permission: Ask first (browser level ask, vault strict)
ui6SetHelp.pit1_consequence: Agents ask before touching a new site, and they use no secret they cannot name. The worst outcome is a few extra clicks from you.
ui6SetHelp.pit2_consequence: Each step up hands the chat more of your computer. Only you can raise it, but once raised it keeps the power until you lower it.
ui6SetHelp.pit3_consequence: An agent can work any site you are logged into, and a form submit on a real site still waits for your approval. Secrets can be used without being read.
ui6SetHelp.pit4_permission: Browser full-no-approvals, vault reveal, org role full access
ui6SetHelp.pit4_consequence: Forms go through without asking and page scripts can read a site's cookies, so an agent can post, buy or send as you. Reveal means it can read your passwords in plaintext.
ui6SetHelp.pit5_permission: Coder mode on, full access, HIL no timeout, auto-approve
ui6SetHelp.pit5_consequence: The agent can run any command and change any file as you, with no asking, so it can delete your home folder as politely as it can fix a typo. Approvals with no timeout wait forever, and auto-approve lets an AI click Approve on your behalf.
